newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: McCarthy to sell motor unit for 218mln rand.
newsitem.headline: McCarthy to sell motor unit for 218mln rand.

text.p: McCarthy Retail Ltd announced on Monday it planned to sell 26 percent of McCarthy Motor Holdings to Imperial Holdings Ltd for 218 million rand with effect from April 1.
The deal was in line with McCarthy Motor Holdings' (MMH) intention to invest in the financial services sector, McCarthy Retail chairman Terry Rosenberg said.
"As a significant shareholder of MMH, Imperial will make its systems and expertise in the financial services arena available to MMH," he said.
Imperial chairman Bill Lynch said the companies would look for synergistic opportunities and areas of co-operation in the fleet management banking, leasing and insurance sectors of the business.
Imperial is a motor retailing operation which also runs a short-term motor insurance company known as Regent Insurance.
While the transaction would increase McCarthy's net asset value per share by more than 10 pct, it would not have a material impact on earnings in the short-term, Rosenberg said.
Lynch said he expected Imperial to benefit from the earnings and growth in the value of its investment in the medium term.
Rosenberg added that the motor holding division would seek a listing on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange as soon as was practicable.
